nena-atlantic-2008.notes: Source 1 is a whole-host crawl of web.cs.dal.ca (personal and research pages) that does not contain the umoncton.ca APICS 2008 pages; no archived copy of the contest site is held. Source 2 corrected to no roles, as the earlier reader did.

sources.evidence: The saved files are personal and research pages on the Dalhousie computer science web host; none of them is from the umoncton.ca APICS 2008 site or any other page of the contest.
Index page headed Atlantic Division Preliminary Contests with one entry per year, where 2008 reads APICS 2008, Oct 17-19, 2008, Universite de Moncton, with a link to that contest's website.
The page has a section headed 2008 UdeM October 17, 2008 – Universite de Moncton with first to fourth place, each marked solved 6 of 6 problems.
PDF of 10 pages holding six numbered problem statements: Cowculations, Pseudoku, Roundabout, Help me read Paul's messages, 2D moving company, Longest subsequence.

sources.evidence: Pages titled APICS Conference 2009 from Dalhousie's computer science site, including an ACM Preliminary Contest - APICS 2009 page with the Friday, October 23 contest hours.

Table of 20 teams with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time, Citation under the heading The 2010 Saint Mary's APICS Contest.
17-page PDF headed APICS/ACM Programming Competition, Friday, October 15, 2010, Problem Set, with problems A to J.

Table of 17 teams with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time under the heading 2014 Atlantic Canadian Preliminary Contest.
13-page PDF of seven numbered problems, Problem 1: Popularity network to Problem 7: The Word Chain Game, matching the known list; no cover.

nena-atlantic-2015.notes: The PDF carries no contest name or date; edition rests on the file name and the problem count.
